inspiration: Staged move picking: the hash-table move is tried first, then captures, then quiet moves; quiet moves are sorted by history scores with a good-quiet cut-off (src/movepick.cpp:282-296; cut-off constant at line 284). For a fight AI: try the last working combo first, then the highest-value option, then the rest, with a cut-off that separates good from weak options.

Two-tier time budget: a soft target from remaining time times a scale factor (src/timeman.cpp:159), and a hard ceiling of 0.8097 of remaining time minus an overhead (timeman.cpp:161). Keep the soft and hard pair: it maps to a per-decision AI budget and to the per-tick NPC budget in row 18.

Swappable evaluation data: the engine exposes an EvalFile option with a default network name (src/engine.cpp:136; src/evaluate.h:36). The fetch script checks a hash and deletes a bad file (scripts/net.sh:18-31). For a learned AI brain: version the weights by hash and fall back cleanly when the file is missing.
Budget top-up: a further 25 percent of the soft budget is added in one branch (timeman.cpp:165). The branch condition was not read, so treat this only as a pointer to a budget top-up rule.

Testing culture: the README says improvements need large numbers of test games run by volunteers. Keep the idea for balance: run many headless simulated fights before a tuning change ships. Not receipted (README contributing section).
No creature, item, zone, effect or sound exists in this donor. The inspiration is all in the AI and budget logic. Nothing here is class A or B.
